body:
[aida:product] #2027 pushed at 53a1382320. Two of three done. And the attribution correction is carried into the PR body as asked.

#2026 MERGED — I saw it land at 0ed4bed7b88f while finishing #2027. That is three tonight from this seat: STORY-1419, BUG-1546, BUG-1441.

#2027 IS PUSHED AND MERGEABLE. The refusal was that the journey test searched each output independently for substrings, so the two projections could disagree on cardinality, target association, ordering or a collapsed row and still pass. Both sections are now parsed into typed edges and compared, with the human/TOON vocabulary correspondence DECLARED in the test rather than assumed — changing either vocabulary fails there now instead of drifting.

THE REMEDY TRANSFER IS IN THE PR BODY explicitly, as you asked, so the reviewer checks it rather than re-deriving it: same shape as BUG-1441's test one layer out, both fixed by parsing the projection instead of searching the document, that one via toon::parse_table and this one inline because a journey test drives the binary rather than linking the library.

THE ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION IS IN THE PR BODY TOO. The seam finding belongs to the `aida drain reviewer` actor, not the reviewer seat that later refused on other grounds, and the verdict file named its last recorder rather than its author. I have stated it that way in writing rather than only in mail, since the mail is where the wrong version lives.

FALSIFIED THREE WAYS AGAINST THE PRODUCTION EMITTER — lossy card buckets red, target association swapped red, duplicate row red, restored green. The middle one is the case the old assertions were blind to: every expected type string still present while the edges pointed at the wrong targets.

AND TWO OF THOSE MUTATIONS FIRST REPORTED GREEN WHILE MEANING NOTHING. One was inserted inside the row-building loop, so three relationships swapped twice and cancelled out; the retry missed its anchor because the closing brace is indented 28 and I had hand-counted 32. I nearly reported the first as a genuine blind spot in my own test. The rule I am now applying: a mutation that produces green must be shown to have actually changed behaviour, or "the test did not catch it" and "the code was never changed" are the same observation.

That is the same boundary error again, pointed at my own instrument rather than at a population: I trusted a null without checking the thing producing it.

ONE PRODUCT OBSERVATION, recorded in the PR body and NOT fixed there. Above five relationships, and without --rels, the human surface prints a COUNT instead of rows while TOON still enumerates. That is a live instance of the "extra collapsed rows" divergence the refusal named — in the product, not the test. The fixture stays at three deliberately so the test measures what it claims. Whether the two surfaces should agree above the threshold is a real question and it is not this spec's to answer; say the word if you want it filed.

VERIFICATION: fmt --check clean, `cargo test -p aida-cli --test journey` 3 passed 0 failed, rebased onto current main (was 21 behind), local branch realigned after the force-push. The gitlab mirror leg rejected the force-push as non-fast-forward, which is expected for a rebase and best-effort by design — flagging it because it is drift you track.

#2033 NEXT, then I stop and report as ruled.
subject: #2027 pushed at 53a1382320 — two of three done, #2026 merged; remedy transfer and attribution both in the PR body
